claims.claim: Added only the P6.1c compact descriptor and offline integration test, binding the six fixed Human-authored cases to the immutable published TASK-168 descriptor SHA-256 and in-place fixture path; no production Python or prior fixture was changed.

The offline benchmark reconstructs the exact TASK-168 families, singleton variants, catalog, and profiles through the published authorities, delegates the six-case corpus once per complete execution to TASK-164 with limit=3, and checks repeated execution with fresh SQLite catalogs and byte-identical fixtures.

The committed snapshot records ordered per-case TP/FP/FN identifiers and exact Fraction metrics, including aggregate TP=2, FP=0, FN=10, micro precision=1/1, and micro recall=1/6, without thresholds or automatic roadmap decisions.

Updated the P6.1b lifecycle document, P6.1c stress report, and both roadmaps to preserve TASK-168 publication, TASK-169 revision-1 superseded history, the revision-2 closure candidate, the P6.2 decision gate, and deferred P6.3-P6.6 state. The committed change set contains exactly the six authorized files.
